slides.title: Welcome to CSS Positioning
slides.content:
# CSS Positioning: Controlling Layout 📍

CSS positioning allows you to manipulate exactly where an element renders on the screen, override normal document flow, pin elements to the viewport, or create sticky navigation bars.

## What you'll master:
- 📜 **Normal Document Flow** - How browsers place elements by default
- 📍 **`static`** - The natural default behavior
- 🔄 **`relative`** - Offsetting an element relative to its original position
- 🎯 **`absolute`** - Precision placement relative to positioned ancestors
- 📌 **`fixed`** - Pinning elements to the browser viewport
- 🧲 **`sticky`** - Dynamic hybrid scroll behavior
- 🥞 **Stacking Contexts & `z-index`** - Layering elements in 3D space

slides.title: Normal Document Flow & Static
slides.content:
# Normal Document Flow & `position: static` 📜

By default, every HTML element has `position: static`.

```css_not
.default-box {
  position: static;
}
```

## How Normal Flow Works:
- Block elements stack vertically from top to bottom.
- Inline elements sit side-by-side from left to right.
- Elements do **not** accept coordinate offsets: properties like `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, and `z-index` have **zero effect** on a static element!

slides.title: Relative Positioning
slides.content:
# Relative Positioning (`position: relative`) 🔄

Setting `position: relative` allows you to offset an element from its original natural position **without** affecting the layout of neighboring elements!

```css_not
.shifted-box {
  position: relative;
  top: 20px;   /* Moves 20px down from original spot */
  left: 30px;  /* Moves 30px right from original spot */
}
```

## Key Characteristics:
- The space the element originally occupied in the document is **preserved** (leaves a blank ghost gap).
- The element merely renders visually shifted over nearby content.
- Crucially: it establishes a **positioning context** for any nested `absolute` children!

Layering with z-index
Understanding Stacking Contexts
slides.content:
# Stacking Contexts Demystified 🏢

Have you ever set `z-index: 999999` and an element STILL appeared behind something with `z-index: 2`? You hit a **Stacking Context** boundary!

A Stacking Context is an isolated layer grouping. An element with `z-index: 9999` inside a parent with `z-index: 1` can **never** appear above a sibling container that has `z-index: 2`!

```
Root Stacking Context
├── Container A (z-index: 1)
│   └── Child (z-index: 999999) <── Still trapped below Container B!
└── Container B (z-index: 2)
```

## What Creates a Stacking Context?
- `position: fixed` or `sticky`
- `position: relative/absolute` with a numeric `z-index`
- Elements with `opacity` less than 1
- Elements with `transform`, `filter`, or `perspective`

slides.title: Sticky Table Headers
Common Positioning Pitfalls
slides.content:
# Positioning Pitfalls to Avoid ⚠️

1. ❌ **Forgetting `position: relative` on parent:** If the parent lacks positioning, an `absolute` child flies all the way to the top of the browser window!
2. ❌ **Using `position: fixed` for whole page layouts:** It removes content from flow and creates overlapping layout bugs on resize.
3. ❌ **High z-index escalation:** Don't start typing `z-index: 9999999`. Define a structured z-index design token scale:
   - Base content: `1`
   - Sticky header: `10`
   - Dropdown menu: `20`
   - Modal backdrop: `40`
   - Modal window: `50`
   - Toast notifications: `100`

Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# CSS Positioning Mastered! 📍

You now have complete control over coordinate placement and visual layering!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **`static`:** Default normal document flow.
- ✅ **`relative`:** Shifted offset; acts as anchor container for children.
- ✅ **`absolute`:** Removed from flow; positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor.
- ✅ **`fixed`:** Pinned directly to the browser viewport.
- ✅ **`sticky`:** Relative scroll until reaching threshold, then pinned.
- ✅ **`z-index` & Stacking:** Requires positioning; governed by parent stacking contexts.
